Two Dominican legends shared one Bronx stage. Luis Vargas, known for more than 40 years as El Rey Supremo de la Bachata, and Monchy of Monchy & Alexandra played Bachatéame New York at Lehman Center for the Performing Arts on Saturday, Nov. 21.

Couples danced in the aisles, phones went up, and the room finished on its feet. For a media company founded by a Dominican-born, Bronx-raised storyteller, this one was personal. Our co-founder Osvaldo "Wally" Rodriguez was on the scene.

Thank you to Leah Grammatica, Alexa Downing and the whole Lehman Center team for having us.

caption_linkedin:
Bachata was once kept off the radio in its own country. On Saturday it filled Lehman Center in the Bronx.

The Innovators Den covered Bachatéame New York with Luis Vargas and Monchy. Three things stood out:

1. Catalogs outlast trends. Luis Vargas is 65, has carried the title El Rey Supremo de la Bachata for more than 40 years, and still fills a room.
2. Crossover has a history. Monchy & Alexandra were the first bachata act on Sábado Gigante, in 2001, and helped take the genre beyond the Dominican Republic.
3. Culture travels with its people. In the Bronx, the audience danced in the aisles.

Thank you to Leah Grammatica, Alexa Downing and the Lehman Center team. Our co-founder Osvaldo "Wally" Rodriguez was on the scene.
